directives.description: Specifies a content handler to run at regular interval. The handler receives a session object as its first argument, it also has access to global objects such as ngx.

directives.name: js_periodic
directives.description: Specifies a content handler to run at regular interval. The handler receives a session object as its first argument, it also has access to global objects such as ngx.

directives.name: js_preload_object
directives.description: Preloads an immutable object at configure time. The `name` is used as a name of the global variable though which the object is available in njs code. If the `name` is not specified, the file name will be used instead. js_preload_object map.json; Here, the `map` is used as a name while accessing the preloaded object.

directives.name: js_preload_object
directives.description: Preloads an immutable object at configure time. The `name` is used as a name of the global variable though which the object is available in njs code. If the `name` is not specified, the file name will be used instead. js_preload_object map.json; Here, the `map` is used as a name while accessing the preloaded object.

directives.name: js_preread
directives.description: Sets an njs function which will be called at the preread phase. Since 0.4.0, a module function can be referenced.

directives.name: js_set
directives.description: Sets an njs `function` for the specified `variable`. Since 0.4.0, a module function can be referenced.

directives.name: js_set
directives.description: Sets an njs `function` for the specified `variable`. Since 0.4.0, a module function can be referenced.

directives.name: js_shared_dict_zone
directives.description: Sets the name and size of the shared memory zone that keeps the key-value dictionary shared between worker processes.

directives.name: js_shared_dict_zone
directives.description: Sets the name and size of the shared memory zone that keeps the key-value dictionary shared between worker processes.

directives.name: js_var
directives.description: Declares a writable variable. The value can contain text, variables, and their combination. The variable is not overwritten after a redirect unlike variables created with the directive.

directives.name: js_var
directives.description: Declares a writable variable. The value can contain text, variables, and their combination.

directives.name: json_max_depth
directives.description: Sets the maximum nesting depth of JSON documents. A document nested deeper is considered invalid. Acceptable values are in the range from 1 to 256.

directives.name: json_set
directives.description: Sets the variable to the value extracted from the JSON document held in the source variable at the given path.

directives.name: keepalive
directives.description: Enables or disables caching of keepalive connections to upstream servers. Since 1.29.7, by default the cache for connections is activated and these connections are not shared between different locations.

directives.name: keepalive_disable
directives.description: Disables keep-alive connections with misbehaving browsers. The browser parameters specify which browsers will be affected. The value `msie6` disables keep-alive connections with old versions of MSIE, once a POST request is received. The value `safari` disables keep-alive connections with Safari and Safari-like browsers on macOS and macOS-like operating systems. The value `none` enables keep-alive connections with all browsers. Prior to version 1.1.18, the value `safari` matched all Safari and Safari-like browsers on all operating systems, and keep-alive connections with them were disabled by default.

directives.name: keepalive_min_timeout
directives.description: Sets a timeout during which a keep-alive client connection will not be closed on the server side for connection reuse or on graceful shutdown of worker processes.

directives.name: keepalive_requests
directives.description: Sets the maximum number of requests that can be served through one keep-alive connection. After the maximum number of requests are made, the connection is closed.

directives.name: keepalive_requests
directives.description: Sets the maximum number of requests that can be served through one keepalive connection. After the maximum number of requests is made, the connection is closed.

directives.name: keepalive_time
directives.description: Limits the maximum time during which requests can be processed through one keep-alive connection. After this time is reached, the connection is closed following the subsequent request processing.

directives.name: keepalive_time
directives.description: Limits the maximum time during which requests can be processed through one keepalive connection. After this time is reached, the connection is closed following the subsequent request processing.

directives.name: keepalive_timeout
directives.description: The first parameter sets a timeout during which a keep-alive client connection will stay open on the server side. The zero value disables keep-alive client connections. The optional second parameter sets a value in the Keep-Alive: timeout=time response header field. Two parameters may differ.

directives.name: keepalive_timeout
directives.description: Sets a timeout during which an idle keepalive connection to an upstream server will stay open.

directives.name: keyval
directives.description: Creates a new $variable whose value is looked up by the key in the key-value database. Matching rules are defined by the `type` parameter of the `keyval_zone` directive. The database is stored in a shared memory zone specified by the `zone` parameter.

directives.name: keyval
directives.description: Creates a new $variable whose value is looked up by the key in the key-value database. Matching rules are defined by the `type` parameter of the `keyval_zone` directive. The database is stored in a shared memory zone specified by the `zone` parameter.

directives.name: keyval_zone
directives.description: Sets the name and size of the shared memory zone that keeps the key-value database. Key-value pairs are managed by the API.

directives.name: keyval_zone
directives.description: Sets the name and size of the shared memory zone that keeps the key-value database. Key-value pairs are managed by the API.

directives.name: large_client_header_buffers
directives.description: Sets the maximum number and size of buffers used for reading large client request header. A request line cannot exceed the size of one buffer, or the error is returned to the client. A request header field cannot exceed the size of one buffer as well, or the error is returned to the client. Buffers are allocated only on demand. By default, the buffer size is equal to 8K bytes. If after the end of request processing a connection is transitioned into the keep-alive state, these buffers are released.

directives.name: least_conn
directives.description: Specifies that a group should use a load balancing method where a request is passed to the server with the least number of active connections, taking into account weights of servers. If there are several such servers, they are tried in turn using a weighted round-robin balancing method.

directives.name: least_conn
directives.description: Specifies that a group should use a load balancing method where a connection is passed to the server with the least number of active connections, taking into account weights of servers. If there are several such servers, they are tried in turn using a weighted round-robin balancing method.

directives.name: least_time
directives.description: Specifies that a group should use a load balancing method where a request is passed to the server with the least average response time and least number of active connections, taking into account weights of servers. If there are several such servers, they are tried in turn using a weighted round-robin balancing method.

directives.name: least_time
directives.description: Specifies that a group should use a load balancing method where a connection is passed to the server with the least average time and least number of active connections, taking into account weights of servers. If there are several such servers, they are tried in turn using a weighted round-robin balancing method.

directives.name: license_pending_token
directives.description: Controls how a renewed JWT license token is handled after it is received from the F5 licensing endpoint. By default, the renewed token is saved and applied immediately.

directives.name: license_token
directives.description: Specifies a JWT license file. By default, the license.jwt file is expected to be at `/etc/nginx/` for Linux or at `/usr/local/etc/nginx/` for FreeBSD.

directives.name: limit_conn
directives.description: Sets the shared memory zone and the maximum allowed number of connections for a given key value. When this limit is exceeded, the server will return the error in reply to a request. For example, the directives limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=addr:10m; server { location /download/ { limit_conn addr 1; } allow only one connection per an IP address at a time. In HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, each concurrent request is considered a separate connection.

directives.name: limit_conn
directives.description: Sets the shared memory zone and the maximum allowed number of connections for a given key value. When this limit is exceeded, the server will close the connection. For example, the directives limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=addr:10m; server { ... limit_conn addr 1; } allow only one connection per an IP address at a time.

directives.name: limit_conn_dry_run
directives.description: Enables the dry run mode. In this mode, the number of connections is not limited, however, in the shared memory zone, the number of excessive connections is accounted as usual.

directives.name: limit_conn_dry_run
directives.description: Enables the dry run mode. In this mode, the number of connections is not limited, however, in the shared memory zone, the number of excessive connections is accounted as usual.

directives.name: limit_conn_log_level
directives.description: Sets the desired logging level for cases when the server limits the number of connections.

directives.name: limit_conn_log_level
directives.description: Sets the desired logging level for cases when the server limits the number of connections.

directives.name: limit_conn_status
directives.description: Sets the status code to return in response to rejected requests.

directives.name: limit_conn_zone
directives.description: Sets parameters for a shared memory zone that will keep states for various keys. In particular, the state includes the current number of connections. The key can contain text, variables, and their combination. Requests with an empty key value are not accounted. Prior to version 1.7.6, a key could contain exactly one variable. Usage example: limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=addr:10m; Here, a client IP address serves as a key. Note that instead of $remote_addr, the $binary_remote_addr variable is used here. The $remote_addr variable’s size can vary from 7 to 15 bytes. The stored state occupies either 32 or 64 bytes of memory on 32-bit platforms and always 64 bytes on 64-bit platforms. The $binary_remote_addr variable’s size is always 4 bytes for IPv4 addresses or 16 bytes for IPv6 addresses. The stored state always occupies 32 or 64 bytes on 32-bit platforms and 64 bytes on 64-bit platforms. One megabyte zone can keep about 32 thousand 32-byte states or about 16 thousand 64-byte states. If the zone storage is exhausted, the server will return the error to all further requests.

directives.name: limit_conn_zone
directives.description: Sets parameters for a shared memory zone that will keep states for various keys. In particular, the state includes the current number of connections. The key can contain text, variables, and their combinations (1.11.2). Connections with an empty key value are not accounted. Usage example: limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=addr:10m; Here, the key is a client IP address set by the `$binary_remote_addr` variable. The size of `$binary_remote_addr` is 4 bytes for IPv4 addresses or 16 bytes for IPv6 addresses. The stored state always occupies 32 or 64 bytes on 32-bit platforms and 64 bytes on 64-bit platforms. One megabyte zone can keep about 32 thousand 32-byte states or about 16 thousand 64-byte states. If the zone storage is exhausted, the server will close the connection.

directives.name: limit_except
directives.description: Limits allowed HTTP methods inside a location. The method parameter can be one of the following: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `MKCOL`, `COPY`, `MOVE`, `OPTIONS`, `PROPFIND`, `PROPPATCH`, `LOCK`, `UNLOCK`, or `PATCH`. Allowing the `GET` method makes the `HEAD` method also allowed. Access to other methods can be limited using the ngx_http_access_module, ngx_http_auth_basic_module, and ngx_http_auth_jwt_module (1.13.10) modules directives: limit_except GET { allow 192.168.1.0/32; deny all; } Please note that this will limit access to all methods except GET and HEAD.

directives.name: limit_rate
directives.description: Limits the rate of response transmission to a client. The rate is specified in bytes per second. The zero value disables rate limiting. The limit is set per a request, and so if a client simultaneously opens two connections, the overall rate will be twice as much as the specified limit.

directives.name: limit_rate_after
directives.description: Sets the initial amount after which the further transmission of a response to a client will be rate limited. Parameter value can contain variables (1.17.0).

directives.name: limit_req
directives.description: Sets the shared memory zone and the maximum burst size of requests. If the requests rate exceeds the rate configured for a zone, their processing is delayed such that requests are processed at a defined rate. Excessive requests are delayed until their number exceeds the maximum burst size in which case the request is terminated with an error. By default, the maximum burst size is equal to zero. For example, the directives limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=one:10m rate=1r/s; server { location /search/ { limit_req zone=one burst=5; } allow not more than 1 request per second at an average, with bursts not exceeding 5 requests.

directives.name: limit_req_dry_run
directives.description: Enables the dry run mode. In this mode, requests processing rate is not limited, however, in the shared memory zone, the number of excessive requests is accounted as usual.

directives.name: limit_req_log_level
directives.description: Sets the desired logging level for cases when the server refuses to process requests due to rate exceeding, or delays request processing. Logging level for delays is one point less than for refusals; for example, if “`limit_req_log_level notice`” is specified, delays are logged with the `info` level.

directives.name: limit_req_status
directives.description: Sets the status code to return in response to rejected requests.

directives.name: limit_req_zone
directives.description: Sets parameters for a shared memory zone that will keep states for various keys. In particular, the state stores the current number of excessive requests. The key can contain text, variables, and their combination. Requests with an empty key value are not accounted. Prior to version 1.7.6, a key could contain exactly one variable. Usage example: limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=one:10m rate=1r/s;

directives.name: limit_zone
directives.description: This directive was made obsolete in version 1.1.8 and was removed in version 1.7.6. An equivalent directive with a changed syntax should be used instead: `limit_conn_zone` $variable `zone`=name:size;

directives.name: lingering_close
directives.description: Controls how nginx closes client connections.

directives.name: lingering_time
directives.description: When is in effect, this directive specifies the maximum time during which nginx will process (read and ignore) additional data coming from a client. After that, the connection will be closed, even if there will be more data.

directives.name: lingering_timeout
directives.description: When is in effect, this directive specifies the maximum waiting time for more client data to arrive. If data are not received during this time, the connection is closed. Otherwise, the data are read and ignored, and nginx starts waiting for more data again. The “wait-read-ignore” cycle is repeated, but no longer than specified by the directive.

directives.name: listen
directives.description: Sets the address and port for IP, or the path for a UNIX-domain socket on which the server will accept requests. Both address and port, or only address or only port can be specified. An address may also be a hostname, for example: listen 127.0.0.1:8000; listen 127.0.0.1; listen 8000; listen *:8000; listen localhost:8000; IPv6 addresses (0.7.36) are specified in square brackets: listen [::]:8000; listen [::1]; UNIX-domain sockets (0.8.21) are specified with the “`unix:`” prefix: listen unix:/var/run/nginx.sock;

directives.name: listen
directives.description: Sets the address and port for the socket on which the server will accept requests. It is possible to specify just the port. The address can also be a hostname, for example: listen 127.0.0.1:110; listen *:110; listen 110; # same as *:110 listen localhost:110; IPv6 addresses (0.7.58) are specified in square brackets: listen [::1]:110; listen [::]:110; UNIX-domain sockets (1.3.5) are specified with the “`unix:`” prefix: listen unix:/var/run/nginx.sock;

directives.name: listen
directives.description: Sets the address and port for the socket on which the server will accept connections. It is possible to specify just the port. The address can also be a hostname, for example: listen 127.0.0.1:12345; listen *:12345; listen 12345; # same as *:12345 listen localhost:12345; IPv6 addresses are specified in square brackets: listen [::1]:12345; listen [::]:12345; UNIX-domain sockets are specified with the “`unix:`” prefix: listen unix:/var/run/nginx.sock;

directives.name: load_module
directives.description: Loads a dynamic module.

directives.name: location
directives.description: Sets configuration depending on a request URI or the value of a variable (1.31.5).

directives.name: lock_file
directives.description: nginx uses the locking mechanism to implement and serialize access to shared memory. On most systems the locks are implemented using atomic operations, and this directive is ignored. On other systems the “lock file” mechanism is used. This directive specifies a prefix for the names of lock files.

directives.name: log_format
directives.description: Specifies log format.

directives.name: log_format
directives.description: Specifies the log format, for example: log_format proxy '$remote_addr [$time_local] ' '$protocol $status $bytes_sent $bytes_received ' '$session_time "$upstream_addr" ' '"$upstream_bytes_sent" "$upstream_bytes_received" "$upstream_connect_time"';

directives.name: log_not_found
directives.description: Enables or disables logging of errors about not found files into .

directives.name: log_subrequest
directives.description: Enables or disables logging of subrequests into .

directives.name: logout_token_hint
directives.description: Adds the `id_token_hint` argument to the Provider's Logout Endpoint when redirecting user during logout. This argument can be required by some OpenID Providers.

directives.name: logout_uri
directives.description: Defines the URI path for initiating session logout. Upon session termination, the user is redirected to Provider's Logout Endpoint or to the post logout page. If neither is configured, the built-in post logout page is displayed.

directives.name: mail
directives.description: Provides the configuration file context in which the mail server directives are specified.

directives.name: map
directives.description: Creates a new variable whose value depends on values of one or more of the source variables specified in the first parameter. Before version 0.9.0 only a single variable could be specified in the first parameter.

directives.name: map
directives.description: Creates a new variable whose value depends on values of one or more of the source variables specified in the first parameter.

directives.name: map_hash_bucket_size
directives.description: Sets the bucket size for the variables hash tables. Default value depends on the processor’s cache line size. The details of setting up hash tables are provided in a separate document.

directives.name: map_hash_bucket_size
directives.description: Sets the bucket size for the variables hash tables. Default value depends on the processor’s cache line size. The details of setting up hash tables are provided in a separate document.

directives.name: map_hash_max_size
directives.description: Sets the maximum size of the variables hash tables. The details of setting up hash tables are provided in a separate document.

directives.name: map_hash_max_size
directives.description: Sets the maximum size of the variables hash tables. The details of setting up hash tables are provided in a separate document.

directives.name: master_process
directives.description: Determines whether worker processes are started. This directive is intended for nginx developers.

directives.name: match
directives.description: Defines the named test set used to verify responses to health check requests.

directives.name: match
directives.description: Defines the named test set used to verify server responses to health checks.

directives.name: max_errors
directives.description: Sets the number of protocol errors after which the connection is closed.

directives.name: max_headers
directives.description: Sets the maximum allowed number of header lines in requests. If this limit is reached, the error is returned.

directives.name: max_ranges
directives.description: Limits the maximum allowed number of ranges in byte-range requests. Requests that exceed the limit are processed as if there were no byte ranges specified. By default, the number of ranges is not limited. The zero value disables the byte-range support completely.

directives.name: memcached_allow_upstream
directives.description: Defines conditions under which access to a memcached server is allowed or denied. If all string parameters are not empty and not equal to “0” then the access is allowed. The conditions are evaluated each time before a connection to a memcached server is established. Parameter values can contain variables: geo $upstream_last_addr $allow { volatile; 10.10.0.0/24 1; } server { listen 127.0.0.1:8080; location / { memcached_pass host:11211; memcached_allow_upstream $allow; ... } }

directives.name: memcached_bind
directives.description: Makes outgoing connections to a memcached server originate from the specified local IP address with an optional port (1.11.2). Parameter value can contain variables (1.3.12). The special value `off` (1.3.12) cancels the effect of the `memcached_bind` directive inherited from the previous configuration level, which allows the system to auto-assign the local IP address and port.

directives.name: memcached_bind_dynamic
directives.description: When enabled, makes the bind operation at each connection attempt.

directives.name: memcached_buffer_size
directives.description: Sets the size of the buffer used for reading the response received from the memcached server. The response is passed to the client synchronously, as soon as it is received.

directives.name: memcached_connect_timeout
directives.description: Defines a timeout for establishing a connection with a memcached server. It should be noted that this timeout cannot usually exceed 75 seconds.

directives.name: memcached_gzip_flag
directives.description: Enables the test for the flag presence in the memcached server response and sets the “`Content-Encoding`” response header field to “`gzip`” if the flag is set.

directives.name: memcached_next_upstream

syntaxes.text: error | timeout | denied | invalid_response | not_found | off ...
syntaxes.line: memcached_next_upstream error | timeout | denied | invalid_response | not_found | off ...;

directives.description: Specifies in which cases a request should be passed to the next server: `error` an error occurred while establishing a connection with the server, passing a request to it, or reading the response header; `timeout` a timeout has occurred while establishing a connection with the server, passing a request to it, or reading the response header; `denied` the server denied the connection (1.29.3); This parameter is available as part of our commercial subscription.

directives.name: memcached_next_upstream_timeout
directives.description: Limits the time during which a request can be passed to the next server. The `0` value turns off this limitation.

directives.name: memcached_next_upstream_tries
directives.description: Limits the number of possible tries for passing a request to the next server. The `0` value turns off this limitation.

directives.name: memcached_pass
directives.description: Sets the memcached server address. The address can be specified as a domain name or IP address, and a port: memcached_pass localhost:11211; or as a UNIX-domain socket path: memcached_pass unix:/tmp/memcached.socket;

directives.name: memcached_read_timeout
directives.description: Defines a timeout for reading a response from the memcached server. The timeout is set only between two successive read operations, not for the transmission of the whole response. If the memcached server does not transmit anything within this time, the connection is closed.

directives.name: memcached_send_timeout
directives.description: Sets a timeout for transmitting a request to the memcached server. The timeout is set only between two successive write operations, not for the transmission of the whole request. If the memcached server does not receive anything within this time, the connection is closed.

directives.name: memcached_socket_keepalive
directives.description: Configures the “TCP keepalive” behavior for outgoing connections to a memcached server. By default, the operating system’s settings are in effect for the socket. If the directive is set to the value “`on`”, the SO_KEEPALIVE socket option is turned on for the socket.

directives.name: merge_slashes
directives.description: Enables or disables compression of two or more adjacent slashes in a URI into a single slash.

directives.name: mgmt
directives.description: Provides the configuration file context in which usage reporting and license management directives are specified.

directives.name: min_delete_depth
directives.description: Allows the DELETE method to remove files provided that the number of elements in a request path is not less than the specified number. For example, the directive min_delete_depth 4; allows removing files on requests /users/00/00/name /users/00/00/name/pic.jpg /users/00/00/page.html and denies the removal of /users/00/00

directives.name: mirror
directives.description: Sets the URI to which an original request will be mirrored. Several mirrors can be specified on the same configuration level.

directives.name: mirror_request_body
directives.description: Indicates whether the client request body is mirrored. When enabled, the client request body will be read prior to creating mirror subrequests. In this case, unbuffered client request body proxying set by the , , , and directives will be disabled. location / { mirror /mirror; mirror_request_body off; proxy_pass http://backend; } location = /mirror { internal; proxy_pass http://log_backend; proxy_pass_request_body off; proxy_set_header Content-Length ""; proxy_set_header X-Original-URI $request_uri; }

directives.name: modern_browser
directives.description: Specifies a version starting from which a browser is considered modern. A browser can be any one of the following: `msie`, `gecko` (browsers based on Mozilla), `opera`, `safari`, or `konqueror`.

directives.name: modern_browser_value
directives.description: Sets a value for the $modern_browser variables.

directives.name: mp4
directives.description: Turns on module processing in a surrounding location.

directives.name: mp4_buffer_size
directives.description: Sets the initial size of the buffer used for processing MP4 files.

directives.name: mp4_limit_rate
directives.description: Limits the rate of response transmission to a client. The rate is limited based on the average bitrate of the MP4 file served. To calculate the rate, the bitrate is multiplied by the specified factor. The special value “`on`” corresponds to the factor of 1.1. The special value “`off`” disables rate limiting. The limit is set per a request, and so if a client simultaneously opens two connections, the overall rate will be twice as much as the specified limit.

directives.name: mp4_limit_rate_after
directives.description: Sets the initial amount of media data (measured in playback time) after which the further transmission of the response to a client will be rate limited.

directives.name: mp4_max_buffer_size
directives.description: During metadata processing, a larger buffer may become necessary. Its size cannot exceed the specified size, or else nginx will return the server error, and log the following message: "/some/movie/file.mp4" mp4 moov atom is too large: 12583268, you may want to increase mp4_max_buffer_size

directives.name: mp4_start_key_frame
directives.description: Forces output video to always start with a key video frame. If the `start` argument does not point to a key frame, initial frames are hidden using an mp4 edit list. Edit lists are supported by major players and browsers such as Chrome, Safari, QuickTime and ffmpeg, partially supported by Firefox.

directives.name: mqtt
directives.description: Enables the MQTT protocol for the given virtual server.

directives.name: mqtt_buffers
directives.description: Sets the number and size of the buffers used for handling MQTT messages, for a single connection.

directives.name: mqtt_preread
directives.description: Enables extracting information from the MQTT CONNECT message at the preread phase.

directives.name: mqtt_rewrite_buffer_size
directives.description: This directive is obsolete since version 1.25.1. The directive should be used instead.

directives.name: mqtt_set_connect
directives.description: Sets the message `field` to the given `value` for CONNECT message. The following fields are supported: `clientid`, `username`, and `password`. The value can contain text, variables, and their combination.

directives.name: msie_padding
directives.description: Enables or disables adding comments to responses for MSIE clients with status greater than 400 to increase the response size to 512 bytes.

directives.name: msie_refresh
directives.description: Enables or disables issuing refreshes instead of redirects for MSIE clients.

directives.name: multi_accept
directives.description: If `multi_accept` is disabled, a worker process will accept one new connection at a time. Otherwise, a worker process will accept all new connections at a time. The directive is ignored if connection processing method is used, because it reports the number of new connections waiting to be accepted.

directives.name: ntlm
directives.description: Allows proxying requests with NTLM Authentication. The upstream connection is bound to the client connection once the client sends a request with the Authorization header field value starting with “`Negotiate`” or “`NTLM`”. Further client requests will be proxied through the same upstream connection, keeping the authentication context.

directives.name: num_map
directives.description: Describes how the values of the specified variable depend on numeric values or numeric value ranges.

directives.name: num_map
directives.description: Describes how the values of the specified variable depend on numeric values or numeric value ranges.

directives.name: oidc_provider
directives.description: Defines an OpenID Provider for use with the directive.

directives.name: open_file_cache
directives.description: Configures a cache that can store: open file descriptors, their sizes and modification times; information on existence of directories; file lookup errors, such as “file not found”, “no read permission”, and so on. Caching of errors should be enabled separately by the directive.

directives.name: open_file_cache_errors
directives.description: Enables or disables caching of file lookup errors by .

directives.name: open_file_cache_events
directives.description: Enables to use kernel events to validate elements. This directive works with the method only. Note that only NetBSD 2.0+ and FreeBSD 6.0+ support events for arbitrary file system types. Other operating systems support events only for essential file systems such as UFS or FFS.

directives.name: open_file_cache_min_uses
directives.description: Sets the minimum number of file accesses during the period configured by the `inactive` parameter of the directive, required for a file descriptor to remain open in the cache.

directives.name: open_file_cache_valid
directives.description: Sets a time after which elements should be validated. is enabled, open file descriptors are checked only once, and then updated right after they get changed. -->

directives.name: open_log_file_cache
directives.description: Defines a cache that stores the file descriptors of frequently used logs whose names contain variables. The directive has the following parameters: `max` sets the maximum number of descriptors in a cache; if the cache becomes full the least recently used (LRU) descriptors are closed `inactive` sets the time after which the cached descriptor is closed if there were no access during this time; by default, 10 seconds `min_uses` sets the minimum number of file uses during the time defined by the `inactive` parameter to let the descriptor stay open in a cache; by default, 1 `valid` sets the time after which it should be checked that the file still exists with the same name; by default, 60 seconds `off` disables caching

directives.name: open_log_file_cache
directives.description: Defines a cache that stores the file descriptors of frequently used logs whose names contain variables. The directive has the following parameters: `max` sets the maximum number of descriptors in a cache; if the cache becomes full the least recently used (LRU) descriptors are closed `inactive` sets the time after which the cached descriptor is closed if there were no access during this time; by default, 10 seconds `min_uses` sets the minimum number of file uses during the time defined by the `inactive` parameter to let the descriptor stay open in a cache; by default, 1 `valid` sets the time after which it should be checked that the file still exists with the same name; by default, 60 seconds `off` disables caching

directives.name: otel_exporter
directives.description: Specifies OTel data export parameters: ` endpoint [(http|https)://]host:port;` OTLP/gRPC endpoint that will accept telemetry data. TLS is supported since 0.1.2. ` trusted_certificate path;` the CA certificates file in PEM format used to verify TLS endpoint (since 0.1.2). Defaults to OS provided CA bundle. `header name value;` a custom HTTP header to add to telemetry export request (since 0.1.2). `interval time;` the maximum interval between two exports, by default is `5` seconds. `batch_size number;` the maximum number of spans to be sent in one batch per worker, by default is `512`. `batch_count number;` the number of pending batches per worker, spans exceeding the limit are dropped, by default is `4`. Example: otel_exporter { endpoint https://otel-example.nginx.com:4317; header X-API-Token "my-token-value"; }

directives.name: otel_resource_attr
directives.description: Sets a custom OTel resource attribute.

directives.name: otel_service_name
directives.description: Sets the “`service.name`” attribute of the OTel resource.

directives.name: otel_span_attr
directives.description: Adds a custom OTel span attribute. The value can contain variables.

directives.name: otel_span_name
directives.description: Defines the name of the OTel span. By default, it is a name of the location for a request. The name can contain variables.

directives.name: otel_trace
directives.description: Enables or disables OpenTelemetry tracing. The directive can also be enabled by specifying a variable: split_clients "$otel_trace_id" $ratio_sampler { 10% on; * off; } server { location / { otel_trace $ratio_sampler; otel_trace_context inject; proxy_pass http://backend; } }

directives.name: otel_trace_context
directives.description: Specifies how to propagate traceparent/tracestate headers: `extract` uses an existing trace context from the request, so that the identifiers of a trace and the parent span are inherited from the incoming request. `inject` adds a new context to the request, overwriting existing headers, if any. `propagate` updates the existing context (combines and ). `ignore` skips context headers processing.

directives.name: output_buffers
directives.description: Sets the number and size of the buffers used for reading a response from a disk. Prior to version 1.9.5, the default value was 1 32k.

directives.name: override_charset
directives.description: Determines whether a conversion should be performed for answers received from a proxied or a FastCGI/uwsgi/SCGI/gRPC server when the answers already carry a charset in the Content-Type response header field. If conversion is enabled, a charset specified in the received response is used as a source charset. It should be noted that if a response is received in a subrequest then the conversion from the response charset to the main request charset is always performed, regardless of the `override_charset` directive setting.

directives.name: pass
directives.description: Sets server address to pass client connection to. The address can be specified as an IP address and a port: pass 127.0.0.1:12345; or as a UNIX-domain socket path: pass unix:/tmp/stream.socket;

directives.name: pcre_jit
directives.description: Enables or disables the use of “just-in-time compilation” (PCRE JIT) for the regular expressions known by the time of configuration parsing.

directives.name: perl
directives.description: Sets a Perl handler for the given location.

directives.name: perl_modules
directives.description: Sets an additional path for Perl modules.

directives.name: perl_require
directives.description: Defines the name of a module that will be loaded during each reconfiguration. Several `perl_require` directives can be present.

directives.name: perl_set
directives.description: Installs a Perl handler for the specified variable.

directives.name: pid
directives.description: Defines a file that will store the process ID of the main process.

directives.name: pkce
directives.description: Explicitly enables or disables PKCE. By default, PKCE is automatically enabled based on OpenID Provider metadata.

directives.name: pop3_auth
directives.description: Sets permitted methods of authentication for POP3 clients. Supported methods are: `plain` USER/PASS, AUTH PLAIN, AUTH LOGIN `apop` APOP. In order for this method to work, the password must be stored unencrypted. `cram-md5` AUTH CRAM-MD5. In order for this method to work, the password must be stored unencrypted. `external` AUTH EXTERNAL (1.11.6).

directives.name: pop3_capabilities
directives.description: Sets the POP3 protocol extensions list that is passed to the client in response to the `CAPA` command. The authentication methods specified in the directive (SASL extension) and STLS are automatically added to this list depending on the directive value.

directives.name: port_in_redirect
directives.description: Enables or disables specifying the port in absolute redirects issued by nginx.

directives.name: post_logout_uri
directives.description: Defines the path or absolute URI to redirect the user to after the logout. The uri must match the configuration on the Provider's side. If the post logout page is served by NGINX, the OIDC module shouldn't be enabled for this location: http { oidc_provider my_idp { ... logout_uri /logout; post_logout_uri /logged_out_page.html; } server { auth_oidc my_idp; location /logged_out_page.html { auth_oidc off; } } }

directives.name: postpone_output
directives.description: If possible, the transmission of client data will be postponed until nginx has at least size bytes of data to send. The zero value disables postponing data transmission.

directives.name: preferred_chain
directives.description: Specifies the preferred certificate chain.

directives.name: preread_buffer_size
directives.description: Specifies a size of the preread buffer.

directives.name: preread_timeout
directives.description: Specifies a timeout of the preread phase.

directives.name: profile
directives.description: Requests the certificate profile name from the ACME server.

directives.name: protocol
directives.description: Sets the protocol for a proxied server. Supported protocols are IMAP, POP3, and SMTP.

directives.name: proxy
directives.description: Sets the HTTP CONNECT proxy used for sending the usage report.

directives.name: proxy
directives.description: Not tested anywhere in the current version.

directives.name: proxy_allow_upstream
directives.description: Defines conditions under which access to a proxied server is allowed or denied. If all string parameters are not empty and not equal to “0” then the access is allowed. The conditions are evaluated each time before a connection to a proxied server is established. Parameter values can contain variables: geo $upstream_last_addr $allow { volatile; 10.10.0.0/24 1; } server { listen 127.0.0.1:8080; location / { proxy_pass localhost:8000; proxy_allow_upstream $allow; ... } }

directives.name: proxy_bind
directives.description: Makes outgoing connections to a proxied server originate from the specified local IP address with an optional port (1.11.2). Parameter value can contain variables (1.3.12). The special value `off` (1.3.12) cancels the effect of the `proxy_bind` directive inherited from the previous configuration level, which allows the system to auto-assign the local IP address and port.

directives.name: proxy_bind
directives.description: Makes outgoing connections to a proxied server originate from the specified local IP address. Parameter value can contain variables (1.11.2). The special value `off` cancels the effect of the `proxy_bind` directive inherited from the previous configuration level, which allows the system to auto-assign the local IP address.

directives.name: proxy_bind_dynamic
directives.description: When enabled, makes the bind operation at each connection attempt.

directives.name: proxy_bind_dynamic
directives.description: When enabled, makes the bind operation at each connection attempt.

directives.name: proxy_buffer
directives.description: Sets the size of the buffer used for proxying. By default, the buffer size is equal to one memory page. Depending on a platform, it is either 4K or 8K.

directives.name: proxy_buffer_size
directives.description: Sets the size of the buffer used for reading the first part of the response received from the proxied server. This part usually contains a small response header; if it exceeds the buffer size, the response is considered invalid. By default, the buffer size is equal to one memory page. This is either 4K or 8K, depending on a platform. It can be made smaller, however.

directives.name: proxy_buffer_size
directives.description: Sets the size of the buffer used for reading data from the proxied server. Also sets the size of the buffer used for reading data from the client.

directives.name: proxy_buffering
directives.description: Enables or disables buffering of responses from the proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_buffers
directives.description: Sets the number and size of the buffers used for reading a response from the proxied server, for a single connection. By default, the buffer size is equal to one memory page. This is either 4K or 8K, depending on a platform.

directives.name: proxy_busy_buffers_size
directives.description: When buffering of responses from the proxied server is enabled, limits the total size of buffers that can be busy sending a response to the client while the response is not yet fully read. In the meantime, the rest of the buffers can be used for reading the response and, if needed, buffering part of the response to a temporary file. By default, size is limited by the size of two buffers set by the and directives.

directives.name: proxy_cache
directives.description: Defines a shared memory zone used for caching. The same zone can be used in several places. Parameter value can contain variables (1.7.9). The `off` parameter disables caching inherited from the previous configuration level.

directives.name: proxy_cache_background_update
directives.description: Allows starting a background subrequest to update an expired cache item, while a stale cached response is returned to the client. Note that it is necessary to allow the usage of a stale cached response when it is being updated.

directives.name: proxy_cache_bypass
directives.description: Defines conditions under which the response will not be taken from a cache. If at least one value of the string parameters is not empty and is not equal to “0” then the response will not be taken from the cache: proxy_cache_bypass $cookie_nocache $arg_nocache$arg_comment; proxy_cache_bypass $http_pragma $http_authorization; Can be used along with the directive.

directives.name: proxy_cache_convert_head
directives.description: Enables or disables the conversion of the “`HEAD`” method to “`GET`” for caching. When the conversion is disabled, the cache key should be configured to include the $request_method.

directives.name: proxy_cache_key
directives.description: Defines a key for caching, for example proxy_cache_key "$host$request_uri $cookie_user"; By default, the directive’s value is close to the string proxy_cache_key $scheme$proxy_host$uri$is_args$args;

directives.name: proxy_cache_lock
directives.description: When enabled, only one request at a time will be allowed to populate a new cache element identified according to the directive by passing a request to a proxied server. Other requests of the same cache element will either wait for a response to appear in the cache or the cache lock for this element to be released, up to the time set by the directive.

directives.name: proxy_cache_lock_age
directives.description: If the last request passed to the proxied server for populating a new cache element has not completed for the specified time, one more request may be passed to the proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_cache_lock_timeout
directives.description: Sets a timeout for . When the time expires, the request will be passed to the proxied server, however, the response will not be cached. Before 1.7.8, the response could be cached.

directives.name: proxy_cache_max_range_offset
directives.description: Sets an offset in bytes for byte-range requests. If the range is beyond the offset, the range request will be passed to the proxied server and the response will not be cached.

directives.name: proxy_cache_methods
directives.description: If the client request method is listed in this directive then the response will be cached. “`GET`” and “`HEAD`” methods are always added to the list, though it is recommended to specify them explicitly. See also the directive.

directives.name: proxy_cache_min_uses
directives.description: Sets the number of requests after which the response will be cached.

directives.name: proxy_cache_path
directives.description: Sets the path and other parameters of a cache. Cache data are stored in files. The file name in a cache is a result of applying the MD5 function to the cache key. The `levels` parameter defines hierarchy levels of a cache: from 1 to 3, each level accepts values 1 or 2. For example, in the following configuration proxy_cache_path /data/nginx/cache levels=1:2 keys_zone=one:10m; file names in a cache will look like this: /data/nginx/cache/c/29/b7f54b2df7773722d382f4809d65029c

directives.name: proxy_cache_purge
directives.description: Defines conditions under which the request will be considered a cache purge request. If at least one value of the string parameters is not empty and is not equal to “0” then the cache entry with a corresponding cache key is removed. The result of successful operation is indicated by returning the response.

directives.name: proxy_cache_revalidate
directives.description: Enables revalidation of expired cache items using conditional requests with the If-Modified-Since and If-None-Match header fields.

directives.name: proxy_cache_use_stale

syntaxes.text: error | timeout | invalid_header | updating | http_500 | http_502 | http_503 | http_504 | http_403 | http_404 | http_429 | off ...
syntaxes.line: proxy_cache_use_stale error | timeout | invalid_header | updating | http_500 | http_502 | http_503 | http_504 | http_403 | http_404 | http_429 | off ...;

directives.description: Determines in which cases a stale cached response can be used during communication with the proxied server. The directive’s parameters match the parameters of the directive.

directives.name: proxy_cache_valid
directives.description: Sets caching time for different response codes. For example, the following directives proxy_cache_valid 200 302 10m; proxy_cache_valid 404 1m; set 10 minutes of caching for responses with codes 200 and 302 and 1 minute for responses with code 404.

directives.name: proxy_connect_timeout
directives.description: Defines a timeout for establishing a connection with a proxied server. It should be noted that this timeout cannot usually exceed 75 seconds.

directives.name: proxy_connect_timeout
directives.description: Defines a timeout for establishing a connection with a proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_cookie_domain
directives.description: Sets a text that should be changed in the `domain` attribute of the Set-Cookie header fields of a proxied server response. Suppose a proxied server returned the Set-Cookie header field with the attribute “`domain=localhost`”. The directive proxy_cookie_domain localhost example.org; will rewrite this attribute to “`domain=example.org`”.

directives.name: proxy_cookie_flags
directives.description: Sets one or more flags for the cookie. The cookie can contain text, variables, and their combinations. The flag can contain text, variables, and their combinations (1.19.8). The `secure`, `httponly`, `samesite=strict`, `samesite=lax`, `samesite=none` parameters add the corresponding flags. The `nosecure`, `nohttponly`, `nosamesite` parameters remove the corresponding flags.

directives.name: proxy_cookie_path
directives.description: Sets a text that should be changed in the `path` attribute of the Set-Cookie header fields of a proxied server response. Suppose a proxied server returned the Set-Cookie header field with the attribute “`path=/two/some/uri/`”. The directive proxy_cookie_path /two/ /; will rewrite this attribute to “`path=/some/uri/`”.

directives.name: proxy_download_rate
directives.description: Limits the speed of reading the data from the proxied server. The rate is specified in bytes per second. The zero value disables rate limiting. The limit is set per a connection, so if nginx simultaneously opens two connections to the proxied server, the overall rate will be twice as much as the specified limit.

directives.name: proxy_force_ranges
directives.description: Enables byte-range support for both cached and uncached responses from the proxied server regardless of the Accept-Ranges field in these responses.

directives.name: proxy_half_close
directives.description: Enables or disables closing each direction of a TCP connection independently (“TCP half-close”). If enabled, proxying over TCP will be kept until both sides close the connection.

directives.name: proxy_headers_hash_bucket_size
directives.description: Sets the bucket size for hash tables used by the and directives. The details of setting up hash tables are provided in a separate document.

directives.name: proxy_headers_hash_max_size
directives.description: Sets the maximum size of hash tables used by the and directives. The details of setting up hash tables are provided in a separate document.

directives.name: proxy_hide_header
directives.description: By default, nginx does not pass the header fields Date, Server, X-Pad, and X-Accel-... from the response of a proxied server to a client. The `proxy_hide_header` directive sets additional fields that will not be passed. If, on the contrary, the passing of fields needs to be permitted, the directive can be used.

directives.name: proxy_http_version
directives.description: Sets the HTTP protocol version for proxying. Since 1.29.7, version 1.1 is used by default. Before 1.29.7, version 1.0 was used by default. Version 1.1 or 2 (1.29.4) is recommended for use with connections and NTLM authentication. Version 2 requires the ngx_http_v2_module module.

directives.name: proxy_ignore_client_abort
directives.description: Determines whether the connection with a proxied server should be closed when a client closes the connection without waiting for a response.

directives.name: proxy_ignore_headers
directives.description: Disables processing of certain response header fields from the proxied server. The following fields can be ignored: X-Accel-Redirect, X-Accel-Expires, X-Accel-Limit-Rate (1.1.6), X-Accel-Buffering (1.1.6), X-Accel-Charset (1.1.6), Expires, Cache-Control, Set-Cookie (0.8.44), and Vary (1.7.7).

directives.name: proxy_intercept_errors
directives.description: Determines whether proxied responses with codes greater than or equal to 300 should be passed to a client or be intercepted and redirected to nginx for processing with the directive.

directives.name: proxy_limit_rate
directives.description: Limits the speed of reading the response from the proxied server. The rate is specified in bytes per second. The zero value disables rate limiting. The limit is set per a request, and so if nginx simultaneously opens two connections to the proxied server, the overall rate will be twice as much as the specified limit. The limitation works only if buffering of responses from the proxied server is enabled. Parameter value can contain variables (1.27.0).

directives.name: proxy_max_temp_file_size
directives.description: When buffering of responses from the proxied server is enabled, and the whole response does not fit into the buffers set by the and directives, a part of the response can be saved to a temporary file. This directive sets the maximum size of the temporary file. The size of data written to the temporary file at a time is set by the directive.

directives.name: proxy_method
directives.description: Specifies the HTTP method to use in requests forwarded to the proxied server instead of the method from the client request. Parameter value can contain variables (1.11.6).

directives.name: proxy_next_upstream

syntaxes.text: error | timeout | denied | invalid_header | http_500 | http_502 | http_503 | http_504 | http_403 | http_404 | http_429 | non_idempotent | off ...
syntaxes.line: proxy_next_upstream error | timeout | denied | invalid_header | http_500 | http_502 | http_503 | http_504 | http_403 | http_404 | http_429 | non_idempotent | off ...;

directives.description: Specifies in which cases a request should be passed to the next server: `error` an error occurred while establishing a connection with the server, passing a request to it, or reading the response header; `timeout` a timeout has occurred while establishing a connection with the server, passing a request to it, or reading the response header; `denied` the server denied the connection (1.29.3); This parameter is available as part of our commercial subscription.

directives.name: proxy_next_upstream
directives.description: When a connection to the proxied server cannot be established, determines whether a client connection will be passed to the next server.

directives.name: proxy_next_upstream_timeout
directives.description: Limits the time during which a request can be passed to the next server. The `0` value turns off this limitation.

directives.name: proxy_next_upstream_timeout
directives.description: Limits the time allowed to pass a connection to the next server. The `0` value turns off this limitation.

directives.name: proxy_next_upstream_tries
directives.description: Limits the number of possible tries for passing a request to the next server. The `0` value turns off this limitation.

directives.name: proxy_next_upstream_tries
directives.description: Limits the number of possible tries for passing a connection to the next server. The `0` value turns off this limitation.

directives.name: proxy_no_cache
directives.description: Defines conditions under which the response will not be saved to a cache. If at least one value of the string parameters is not empty and is not equal to “0” then the response will not be saved: proxy_no_cache $cookie_nocache $arg_nocache$arg_comment; proxy_no_cache $http_pragma $http_authorization; Can be used along with the directive.

directives.name: proxy_pass
directives.description: Sets the protocol and address of a proxied server and an optional URI to which a location should be mapped. As a protocol, “`http`” or “`https`” can be specified. The address can be specified as a domain name or IP address, and an optional port: proxy_pass http://localhost:8000/uri/; or as a UNIX-domain socket path specified after the word “`unix`” and enclosed in colons: proxy_pass http://unix:/tmp/backend.socket:/uri/;

directives.name: proxy_pass
directives.description: Sets the address of a proxied server. The address can be specified as a domain name or IP address, and a port: proxy_pass localhost:12345; or as a UNIX-domain socket path: proxy_pass unix:/tmp/stream.socket;

directives.name: proxy_pass_error_message
directives.description: Indicates whether to pass the error message obtained during the authentication on the backend to the client.

directives.name: proxy_pass_header
directives.description: Permits passing otherwise disabled header fields from a proxied server to a client.

directives.name: proxy_pass_request_body
directives.description: Indicates whether the original request body is passed to the proxied server. location /x-accel-redirect-here/ { proxy_method GET; proxy_pass_request_body off; proxy_set_header Content-Length ""; proxy_pass ... } See also the and directives.

directives.name: proxy_pass_request_headers
directives.description: Indicates whether the header fields of the original request are passed to the proxied server. location /x-accel-redirect-here/ { proxy_method GET; proxy_pass_request_headers off; proxy_pass_request_body off; proxy_pass ... } See also the and directives.

directives.name: proxy_pass_trailers
directives.description: Permits passing trailer fields from a proxied server to a client.

directives.name: proxy_password
directives.description: Sets the password used for authentication on the proxy.

directives.name: proxy_protocol
directives.description: Enables the PROXY protocol for connections to a backend. The `on` parameter enables version 1 of the PROXY protocol (text format). The `v2` parameter (1.31.4) enables version 2 of the PROXY protocol (binary format).

directives.name: proxy_protocol
directives.description: Enables the PROXY protocol for connections to a proxied server. The `on` parameter enables version 1 of the PROXY protocol (text format). The `v2` parameter (1.31.4) enables version 2 of the PROXY protocol (binary format).

directives.name: proxy_protocol_timeout
directives.description: Specifies a timeout for reading the PROXY protocol header to complete. If no entire header is transmitted within this time, the connection is closed.

directives.name: proxy_read_timeout
directives.description: Defines a timeout for reading a response from the proxied server. The timeout is set only between two successive read operations, not for the transmission of the whole response. If the proxied server does not transmit anything within this time, the connection is closed.

directives.name: proxy_redirect
directives.description: Sets the text that should be changed in the Location and Refresh header fields of a proxied server response. Suppose a proxied server returned the header field “`Location: http://localhost:8000/two/some/uri/`”. The directive proxy_redirect http://localhost:8000/two/ http://frontend/one/; will rewrite this string to “`Location: http://frontend/one/some/uri/`”.

directives.name: proxy_request_buffering
directives.description: Enables or disables buffering of a client request body.

directives.name: proxy_request_dynamic
directives.description: Enables or disables creation of a separate request instance for each proxied server. By default, a single request is used for all proxied servers. If enabled, a separate request instance is created, allowing per-server request customization. For example, the server-specific Host request header field can be set: proxy_request_dynamic on; proxy_set_header Host $upstream_last_server_name;

directives.name: proxy_requests
directives.description: Sets the number of client datagrams at which binding between a client and existing UDP stream session is dropped. After receiving the specified number of datagrams, next datagram from the same client starts a new session. The session terminates when all client datagrams are transmitted to a proxied server and the expected number of responses is received, or when it reaches a timeout.

directives.name: proxy_responses
directives.description: Sets the number of datagrams expected from the proxied server in response to a client datagram if the UDP protocol is used. The number serves as a hint for session termination. By default, the number of datagrams is not limited.

directives.name: proxy_send_lowat
directives.description: If the directive is set to a non-zero value, nginx will try to minimize the number of send operations on outgoing connections to a proxied server by using either NOTE_LOWAT flag of the method, or the SO_SNDLOWAT socket option, with the specified size.

directives.name: proxy_send_timeout
directives.description: Sets a timeout for transmitting a request to the proxied server. The timeout is set only between two successive write operations, not for the transmission of the whole request. If the proxied server does not receive anything within this time, the connection is closed.

directives.name: proxy_session_drop
directives.description: Enables terminating all sessions to a proxied server after it was removed from the group or marked as permanently unavailable. This can occur because of re-resolve or with the API `DELETE` command. A server can be marked as permanently unavailable if it is considered unhealthy or with the API `PATCH` command. Each session is terminated when the next read or write event is processed for the client or proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_set_body
directives.description: Allows redefining the request body passed to the proxied server. The value can contain text, variables, and their combination.

directives.name: proxy_set_header
directives.description: Allows redefining or appending fields to the request header passed to the proxied server. The value can contain text, variables, and their combinations. These directives are inherited from the previous configuration level if and only if there are no `proxy_set_header` directives defined on the current level.

directives.name: proxy_smtp_auth
directives.description: Enables or disables user authentication on the SMTP backend using the `AUTH` command.

directives.name: proxy_socket_keepalive
directives.description: Configures the “TCP keepalive” behavior for outgoing connections to a proxied server. By default, the operating system’s settings are in effect for the socket. If the directive is set to the value “`on`”, the SO_KEEPALIVE socket option is turned on for the socket.

directives.name: proxy_socket_keepalive
directives.description: Configures the “TCP keepalive” behavior for outgoing connections to a proxied server. By default, the operating system’s settings are in effect for the socket. If the directive is set to the value “`on`”, the SO_KEEPALIVE socket option is turned on for the socket.

directives.name: proxy_socket_rcvbuf
directives.description: Sets the receive buffer size (the SO_RCVBUF option) for outgoing connections to a proxied server. The special value `0` cancels the effect of the `proxy_socket_rcvbuf` directive inherited from the previous configuration level, which allows keeping the operating system’s settings in effect for the socket.

directives.name: proxy_socket_rcvbuf
directives.description: Sets the receive buffer size (the SO_RCVBUF option) for outgoing connections to a proxied server. The special value `0` cancels the effect of the `proxy_socket_rcvbuf` directive inherited from the previous configuration level, which allows keeping the operating system’s settings in effect for the socket.

directives.name: proxy_socket_sndbuf
directives.description: Sets the send buffer size (the SO_SNDBUF option) for outgoing connections to a proxied server. The special value `0` cancels the effect of the `proxy_socket_sndbuf` directive inherited from the previous configuration level, which allows keeping the operating system’s settings in effect for the socket.

directives.name: proxy_socket_sndbuf
directives.description: Sets the send buffer size (the SO_SNDBUF option) for outgoing connections to a proxied server. The special value `0` cancels the effect of the `proxy_socket_sndbuf` directive inherited from the previous configuration level, which allows keeping the operating system’s settings in effect for the socket.

directives.name: proxy_ssl
directives.description: Enables the SSL/TLS protocol for connections to a proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_alpn
directives.description: Specifies the list of protocols to advertise via the ALPN extension when establishing a connection with the proxied server. For example: proxy_ssl_alpn h2 http/1.1;

directives.name: proxy_ssl_certificate
directives.description: Specifies a file with the certificate in the PEM format used for authentication to a proxied HTTPS server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_certificate
directives.description: Specifies a file with the certificate in the PEM format used for authentication to a proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_certificate_cache
directives.description: Defines a cache that stores SSL certificates and secret keys specified with variables.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_certificate_cache
directives.description: Defines a cache that stores SSL certificates and secret keys specified with variables.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_certificate_key
directives.description: Specifies a file with the secret key in the PEM format used for authentication to a proxied HTTPS server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_certificate_key
directives.description: The value `store`:scheme:id can be specified instead of the file (1.29.0), which is used to load a secret key with a specified id and OpenSSL provider registered URI scheme, such as `pkcs11`.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_ciphers
directives.description: Specifies the enabled ciphers for requests to a proxied HTTPS server. The ciphers are specified in the format understood by the OpenSSL library.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_ciphers
directives.description: Specifies the enabled ciphers for connections to a proxied server. The ciphers are specified in the format understood by the OpenSSL library.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_conf_command
directives.description: Sets arbitrary OpenSSL configuration commands when establishing a connection with the proxied HTTPS server. The directive is supported when using OpenSSL 1.0.2 or higher.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_conf_command
directives.description: Sets arbitrary OpenSSL configuration commands when establishing a connection with the proxied server. The directive is supported when using OpenSSL 1.0.2 or higher.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_crl
directives.description: Specifies a file with revoked certificates (CRL) in the PEM format used to verify the certificate of the proxied HTTPS server. When using intermediate certificates, their CRLs should be specified in the same file.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_crl
directives.description: Specifies a file with revoked certificates (CRL) in the PEM format used to verify the certificate of the proxied server. When using intermediate certificates, their CRLs should be specified in the same file.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_key_log
directives.description: Enables logging of proxied HTTPS server connection SSL keys and specifies the path to the key log file. Keys are logged in the SSLKEYLOGFILE format compatible with Wireshark.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_key_log
directives.description: Enables logging of proxied server connection SSL keys and specifies the path to the key log file. Keys are logged in the SSLKEYLOGFILE format compatible with Wireshark.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_name
directives.description: Allows overriding the server name used to verify the certificate of the proxied HTTPS server and to be passed through SNI when establishing a connection with the proxied HTTPS server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_name
directives.description: Allows overriding the server name used to verify the certificate of the proxied server and to be passed through SNI when establishing a connection with the proxied server. The server name can also be specified using variables (1.11.3).

directives.name: proxy_ssl_password_file
directives.description: Specifies a file with passphrases for secret keys where each passphrase is specified on a separate line. Passphrases are tried in turn when loading the key.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_password_file
directives.description: Specifies a file with passphrases for secret keys where each passphrase is specified on a separate line. Passphrases are tried in turn when loading the key.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_protocols
directives.description: Enables the specified protocols for requests to a proxied HTTPS server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_protocols
directives.description: Enables the specified protocols for connections to a proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_server_name
directives.description: Enables or disables passing of the server name through TLS Server Name Indication extension (SNI, RFC 6066) when establishing a connection with the proxied HTTPS server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_server_name
directives.description: Enables or disables passing of the server name through TLS Server Name Indication extension (SNI, RFC 6066) when establishing a connection with the proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_session_reuse
directives.description: Determines whether SSL sessions can be reused when working with the proxied server. If the errors “`digest check failed`” appear in the logs, try disabling session reuse.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_session_reuse
directives.description: Determines whether SSL sessions can be reused when working with the proxied server. If the errors “`digest check failed`” appear in the logs, try disabling session reuse.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_trusted_certificate
directives.description: Specifies a file with trusted CA certificates in the PEM format used to verify the certificate of the proxied HTTPS server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_trusted_certificate
directives.description: Specifies a file with trusted CA certificates in the PEM format used to verify the certificate of the proxied server.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_verify
directives.description: Enables or disables verification of the proxied HTTPS server certificate.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_verify
directives.description: Enables or disables verification of the proxied server certificate.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_verify_depth
directives.description: Sets the verification depth in the proxied HTTPS server certificates chain.

directives.name: proxy_ssl_verify_depth
directives.description: Sets the verification depth in the proxied server certificates chain.

directives.name: proxy_store
directives.description: Enables saving of files to a disk. The `on` parameter saves files with paths corresponding to the directives or . The `off` parameter disables saving of files. In addition, the file name can be set explicitly using the string with variables: proxy_store /data/www$original_uri;

directives.name: proxy_store_access
directives.description: Sets access permissions for newly created files and directories, e.g.: proxy_store_access user:rw group:rw all:r;

directives.name: proxy_temp_file_write_size
directives.description: Limits the size of data written to a temporary file at a time, when buffering of responses from the proxied server to temporary files is enabled. By default, size is limited by two buffers set by the and directives. The maximum size of a temporary file is set by the directive.

directives.name: proxy_temp_path
directives.description: Defines a directory for storing temporary files with data received from proxied servers. Up to three-level subdirectory hierarchy can be used underneath the specified directory. For example, in the following configuration proxy_temp_path /spool/nginx/proxy_temp 1 2; a temporary file might look like this: /spool/nginx/proxy_temp/7/45/00000123457

directives.name: proxy_timeout
directives.description: Sets the timeout between two successive read or write operations on client or proxied server connections. If no data is transmitted within this time, the connection is closed.

directives.name: proxy_timeout
directives.description: Sets the timeout between two successive read or write operations on client or proxied server connections. If no data is transmitted within this time, the connection is closed.

directives.name: proxy_upload_rate
directives.description: Limits the speed of reading the data from the client. The rate is specified in bytes per second. The zero value disables rate limiting. The limit is set per a connection, so if the client simultaneously opens two connections, the overall rate will be twice as much as the specified limit.

directives.name: proxy_username
directives.description: Sets the user name used for authentication on the proxy.

directives.name: queue
directives.description: If an upstream server cannot be selected immediately while processing a request, the request will be placed into the queue. The directive specifies the maximum number of requests that can be in the queue at the same time. If the queue is filled up, or the server to pass the request to cannot be selected within the time period specified in the `timeout` parameter, the error will be returned to the client.

directives.name: quic_active_connection_id_limit
directives.description: Sets the QUIC `active_connection_id_limit` transport parameter value. This is the maximum number of client connection IDs which can be stored on the server.

directives.name: quic_bpf
directives.description: Enables routing of QUIC packets using eBPF. When enabled, this allows supporting QUIC connection migration.

directives.name: quic_gso
directives.description: Enables sending in optimized batch mode using segmentation offloading.

directives.name: quic_host_key
directives.description: Sets a file with the secret key used to encrypt stateless reset and address validation tokens. By default, a random key is generated on each reload. Tokens generated with old keys are not accepted.

directives.name: quic_retry
directives.description: Enables the QUIC Address Validation feature. This includes sending a new token in a `Retry` packet or a `NEW_TOKEN` frame and validating a token received in the `Initial` packet.

directives.name: random
directives.description: Specifies that a group should use a load balancing method where a request is passed to a randomly selected server, taking into account weights of servers.

directives.name: random
directives.description: Specifies that a group should use a load balancing method where a connection is passed to a randomly selected server, taking into account weights of servers.

directives.name: random_index
directives.description: Enables or disables module processing in a surrounding location.

directives.name: read_ahead
directives.description: Sets the amount of pre-reading for the kernel when working with file.

directives.name: real_ip_header
directives.description: Defines the request header field whose value will be used to replace the client address.

directives.name: real_ip_recursive
directives.description: If recursive search is disabled, the original client address that matches one of the trusted addresses is replaced by the last address sent in the request header field defined by the directive. If recursive search is enabled, the original client address that matches one of the trusted addresses is replaced by the last non-trusted address sent in the request header field.

directives.name: recursive_error_pages
directives.description: Enables or disables doing several redirects using the directive. The number of such redirects is limited.

directives.name: redirect_uri
directives.description: Defines the Redirection URI path for post-authentication redirects expected by the module from the OpenID Provider. The uri must match the configuration on the Provider's side.

directives.name: referer_hash_bucket_size
directives.description: Sets the bucket size for the valid referers hash tables. The details of setting up hash tables are provided in a separate document.

directives.name: referer_hash_max_size
directives.description: Sets the maximum size of the valid referers hash tables. The details of setting up hash tables are provided in a separate document.

directives.name: request_pool_size
directives.description: Allows accurate tuning of per-request memory allocations. This directive has minimal impact on performance and should not generally be used.

directives.name: reset_timedout_connection
directives.description: Enables or disables resetting timed out connections and connections closed with the non-standard code 444 (1.15.2). The reset is performed as follows. Before closing a socket, the SO_LINGER option is set on it with a timeout value of 0. When the socket is closed, TCP RST is sent to the client, and all memory occupied by this socket is released. This helps avoid keeping an already closed socket with filled buffers in a FIN_WAIT1 state for a long time.

directives.name: resolver
directives.description: Configures name servers used to resolve usage reporting endpoint name. By default, the system resolver is used.

directives.name: resolver
directives.description: Configures name servers used to resolve names of upstream servers into addresses, for example: resolver 127.0.0.1 [::1]:5353; The address can be specified as a domain name or IP address, with an optional port (1.3.1, 1.2.2). If port is not specified, the port 53 is used. Name servers are queried in a round-robin fashion. Before version 1.1.7, only a single name server could be configured. Specifying name servers using IPv6 addresses is supported starting from versions 1.3.1 and 1.2.2.

directives.name: resolver
